thingsToDo.title: Hanalei Bay
thingsToDo.description: Hanalei Bay is a bay in or near Hanalei, Hawaii. Hanalei Bay is a large semicircular bay on Kauaʻi's north shore, with beaches framed by mountain ridges and river-fed wetlands. The bay is a defining geographic feature of the Hanalei area and supports surfing, paddling, and shoreline recreation. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation.

thingsToDo.title: Hanalei Pier
thingsToDo.description: Hanalei Pier is a historic pier in or near Hanalei, Hawaii. Hanalei Pier is a historic pier in Hanalei Bay that has served shipping, fishing, and community uses since the late nineteenth century. The structure is listed as part of Hanalei's coastal heritage landscape and remains a focal public landmark. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation.

thingsToDo.title: Waiʻoli Mission District
thingsToDo.description: Waiʻoli Mission District is a historic district in or near Hanalei, Hawaii. The Waiʻoli Mission District in Hanalei preserves nineteenth-century missionary-era buildings, including Waiʻoli Huiʻia Church and mission house structures. The district documents early Protestant mission history on Kauaʻi and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation.

thingsToDo.title: Hanalei Valley Lookout
thingsToDo.description: Hanalei Valley Lookout is a scenic overlook in or near Hanalei, Hawaii. Hanalei Valley Lookout is an overlook above Hanalei's taro fields and wetland plain near the Kūhiō Highway corridor. The viewpoint is widely used to interpret valley agriculture, floodplain geography, and mountain-to-bay landscape relationships on Kauaʻi. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation. Its present-day access and management context shape how residents and visitors use the area.

thingsToDo.title: Hā‘ena State Park
thingsToDo.description: Hā‘ena State Park is a state park in or near Hanalei, Hawaii. Hā‘ena State Park is a coastal state park on Kauaʻi that includes beaches, sea cliffs, and access to the Kalalau Trail. The park protects significant natural and cultural sites and operates with managed-entry systems for conservation and visitor safety. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Hanalei?
faq.a: Two to three days is enough for core Hanalei highlights plus one or two local experiences.

faq.q: Should I book tours ahead in Hanalei?
faq.a: Yes—advance booking is recommended for weekends, holidays, and top-rated operators.
